diagnosis: All four rollouts are structurally identical: every agent reveals its hidden fact (PF1–PF4) and the settlement correctly cites all of them in justification_fact_ids, yet checks C2, C3, C6, C9, C10, and C11 fail 0/4 while C4, C5, C7, C8, and P1 pass 4/4. The agents disclose the right content and the settlement encodes the right decisions, so this is an ENCODING MISMATCH on six checks, not a disclosure or telepathy problem. Specifically, C2/C3 (PF1, module M-17 replacement), C6/C10 (PF3, administrative-workflow-only and diagnostic-claim removal), C9 (PF2, 30-day deletion), and C11 (PF4, annual customer audit right) all fail despite the settlement decisions containing matching values (e.g., content_deletion_days_after_termination=30, permitted_intended_use_description containing "administrative workflow tool only", annual_customer_audit_right_required=true). The check wording or field-name expectations for these six checks do not align with how the model naturally encodes the information in the settlement.

C6.why: The planned clinical-triage wording would remain in the launch materials without PF3, while PF3 changes the permitted description to administrative workflow only and requires removal of diagnostic claims.

C10.why: The planned clinical-triage wording would remain in the launch materials without PF3, while PF3 changes the permitted description to administrative workflow only and requires removal of diagnostic claims.

C2.why: The production build would otherwise remain on the standard proprietary path; PF1 changes the required software choice to replacing exactly module M-17 before external customer access.
